restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, with origins t_j drawn as fresh randomness (two independent uniform random 256-bit words per coset, Section 6.1) and the fixed Gray order of each coset.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1626: a six-round permutation is one unit, every other operation 1/1626 (no permutation call is made: verification evaluates the six rounds in 1108 word operations per message, constant-folded and round-5 output-pruned); generated straight-line code with immediate addresses, its generation charged in preprocessing (proof.md Section 5.1). N = G F_g + G (4664 2^40 + 175 (2^40 - 1)) + G S_g + 9 Q + 2302 R140 + (2^70 + 16) = 13723279081462951266323661654033971144284 word operations (Section 10), with the constant-folded bit-sliced setup S_g = 6723180993068 per group (Section 6.5) and verification at most 2302 (Section 7); time_log2 = 122.66664 is log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12266663 <= N^100000 < 1626^100000 2^12266664.

Memory below 2^141 words, 2^146 bytes: a direct sparse array of 2^140 words that is never initialized (the sparse-set table, indexed by the candidate identifier, is correct for any initial memory, Lemma 8), a dense array of Q words, coset records (the retained random origins), a work region with a per-group buffer of 175 (2^40 - 1) words, and generated code (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 word operations (below 2^59.34 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, constants, byte tables, the certificate and the search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh coins (the random coset origins, drawn by a leader step charged at its 11 operations per coset and 5 per group) and rests on one declared heuristic, H_coset: over those coins the occupancy, key-match and triple bounds of proof.md Section 9 hold (Section 12). Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40 (780-polarization certificate, recomputed by the experiment), degree at most 8 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order finite differences and of their initialization, the sparse-set table for arbitrary initial memory, the duplicate-coset bound C(256 G, 2) 2^-280 < 2.5e-32 in the failure budget, detection up to a bounded triple event, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. The three declared experiments execute the schedule at a reduced size (one group of 256 cosets with origins from the trials' own coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, the full 140-bit key and table) through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md. fes-campaign-reduced checks for a full collision (none expected); hcoset-within16 and hcoset-cross16 test a reduced-width form of H_coset on the run's own digests (proof.md Section 12.2): organizer-checked 16-bit mask events within one coset and across two cosets, and pair counts that must lie in stated intervals. A mask success is not a collision; nothing about cost is inferred.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. CAMP's coins are the C = 256 G coset origins t_j (G = 1202250025869134545910402), independent and uniform on F_2^320, each drawn from two calls of the cost model's primitive 'independent uniform random 256-bit word' (proof.md Section 6.1). For the Q = 2^48 G messages they generate, with the fixed Gray enumeration of span(W40) inside each coset in CAMP's order, let D be the event that the C cosets are distinct (Pr[not D] <= C(C, 2) 2^-280 < 2.5e-32, proved, Lemma 7), F1 the event that no two messages share a digest, X the number of unordered pairs with equal 140-bit keys and Y the number of bad triples (Lemma 9). Assume, over the coins: (a) Pr[F1 | D] <= 1/T40 with T40 = sum_{k<=40} lambda^k/k! and lambda = Q(Q - 1)/2^257; (b) E[X | D] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141 and Var[X | D] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141; (c) E[Y | D] <= lambda (Q - 2)/2^140. These are the values that independent uniform digests of distinct messages give. Then the failure probability over the fresh coins is at most Pr[not D] + 1/T40 + 1/kappa (Chebyshev at the verification cap R140 = r140 + ceil(sqrt(kappa r140)), kappa = 19345871228983, r140 = ceil(Q(Q - 1)/2^141)) + lambda (Q - 2)/2^140 (Markov) < 61/100 (exact rational comparison; G is the least group count for which it holds at this kappa), so the success probability is greater than 0.3900000000000000000000000000469 (proof.md Section 9).
heuristics.scope: The randomized campaign at full size: C = 256 G independent uniform coset origins drawn by the algorithm, complete 40-dimensional cosets of span(W40) in the fixed Gray order, the full 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key projection, conditioned on distinct cosets. The success probability is over these fresh coins for the fixed target. Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the sparse-set table, the duplicate-coset bound and every operation count are proved in proof.md Sections 3 to 7, 9 and 10.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence on the six-round target. (1) Organizer-executed at every run of the declared experiments hcoset-within16 and hcoset-cross16 (proof.md Sections 12.2 and 13): on 2^17 digests of 256 cosets whose origins come from the organizer's trial seeds, the pair counts inside one coset at 16 bits and across cosets at 16 and 24 bits must lie within 4 standard deviations of their exact uniform expectations (511, 130560, 510) or the run fails, and the organizer recomputes every returned 16-bit agreeing pair, inside one coset (512 points) and across two independent-origin cosets (256 x 256 points); the exact uniform success probabilities per trial are 0.864841510863844 and 0.632121969489614, with pass intervals [200, 243] and [131, 192] successes of 256. (2) GPU, preregistered, our runs (protocols hashed before the runs; one-sided pass rule at 4 sigma; no reruns; proof.md Section 12.1 and Appendix A, with the GPU-versus-organizer digest checks kept as a printout in A.6): batch W, 2^34 digests per run with uniform random coset origins in one 34-dimensional coset (1/64 of a complete coset) or 1024 cosets of dimension 24, exact equal-pair counts of 36- to 64-bit projections (whole digest lanes and two-lane projections), 96 six-round field counts with z from -3.14 to +2.16, PASS; batches 1 to 3, 17 runs of 2^30 digests, 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections of each digest lane, 13 with random origins, every count within 2.1 sigma; five-round runs as context. (3) Sensitivity (proof.md Section 12.3): if the pair-collision rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the success at this N stays above 0.386976, 0.374732, 0.359083 and 0.309746 for eps = 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.25, and 0.39 is restored at 0.00731, 0.03728, 0.07659 and 0.20921 extra log2 cost (integer certificates). The extrapolation is from projections of at most 64 bits, 2^17 to 2^34 messages and 9- to 34-dimensional sub-cosets to the full 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key, Q messages and complete 40-dimensional cosets; the full 256-bit collision event is the premise, not a measurement.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 16 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure. The organizer-executed tests reach 16 and 24 bits and 2^17 digests per run; the GPU evidence, our runs validated against the organizer reference, reaches 64-bit projections, 2^34 digests and 34-dimensional sub-cosets. No test reaches 256 bits, complete cosets or Q messages, none measures the key-match variance or the triple rate at 140 bits, and no full collision is observed. The time bound is computed at the uniform pair rate; a shortfall eps needs the larger G of proof.md Section 12.3.
